question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\,Γ(\frac{9}{2}) & =\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\cdot \frac{7}{2}\cdot Γ(\frac{7}{2}) \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\cdot \frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}Γ(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\cdot \frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}Γ(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\cdot \frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}Γ(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{16\sqrt{\pi }}{15}\cdot \frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi } \\  & =7\pi \end{aligned}
$$
